_comment: Every file served from the static bucket, and the S3 key it lands on.
One source of truth on purpose: service/static/sync.sh uploads exactly
this list and tests/test_static_assets.py checks it against what the two
HTML pages actually reference. A file referenced by a page but missing
here is the /app.js bug again -- the page loads and one feature is dead
-- which has shipped five times in this project against the ALB.
Keys mirror the URL paths exactly, because every reference in the pages
is RELATIVE (src="app.js", href="icons/icon-192.png"). Renaming a key
silently 404s the reference.
Note 'admin', 'metrics' and 'lab' have no extension: they are one page,
control/lab.html (3.132 Stage 4), published at all three paths so the
consoles' old links keep working -- the page picks its tab from the path.
The keys are extensionless, so the content type is set explicitly rather
than guessed.
cache: 'none' for the scripts, stylesheets and pages, matching the
no-cache headers robot/server.py and admin_server.py already send --
this project deliberately does not use content-hashed filenames, so a
cached app.js is a stale UI nobody can explain. Icons and the manifest
are immutable in practice and cache for a day.
ORDER IS UPLOAD ORDER (sync.sh puts them one by one). The twin's modules
(js/) go before app.js, which imports them, and each before any module
that imports it: during a sync a phone must never get an app.js that
imports a key not yet in the bucket -- one failed import stops the whole
module graph and the page is dead (3.132 Stage 2B). Then index.html,
after the modules (its modulepreload must not fetch one not yet there:
CloudFront caches a 403 for seconds) and before app.js (an old page
loads app.js as a classic script, where an import line is a
SyntaxError).
